description: Intent i026 (branch=timer-dwork-softirq-lock, snapshot s11) complete. FINDING: net/bridge/br_multicast.c:886-916 — br_multicast_enable_port (lock at 890) and br_multicast_disable_port (lock at 901, unlock 913) take br->multicast_lock with plain spin_lock() in process context (reached from br_stp.c:476 and br_stp_if.c br_stp_enable_port/br_stp_disable_port via netlink/sysfs port-state change in br.c/br_if.c), while the same lock object (spin_lock_init at br_multicast.c:1810) is acquired plainly inside TIMER_SOFTIRQ callbacks: br_multicast_group_expired (147, timer_setup at 460), br_multicast_port_group_expired (205, timer_setup at 491), br_multicast_router_expired (632, timer_setup at 828), br_multicast_local_router_expired (660, timer_setup at 1811), br_multicast_querier_expired (timer_setup at 1813/1818) and br_multicast_query_expired (1759, wired via br_ip4/br_ip6_multicast_query_expired timer_setup at 1815/1820). Sibling process sites on the SAME lock correctly use spin_lock_bh (853, 1929, 1946, 2053, 2090, 2103, 2142, 2161), proving mixed discipline and the missing bottom-half disable — the timer-softirq analogue of the ks7010 seed. Impact: a TIMER_SOFTIRQ on the same CPU spins forever on the lock while the preempted holder can never resume (soft lockup / RCU stall / bridge multicast stall DoS). Trigger is attacker-influenced concurrency (IGMP/MLD traffic arming timers plus a port-state/link event), not data. Confidence medium; static analysis only. Safe candidates: tun.c, garp.c, mrp.c, bcm63xx_enet.c, libiscsi.c (this snapshot's iscsi sites use _bh on process side). Unresolved for follow-up: iwlwifi pcie/tx.c txq->lock stuck timer, cxgb4 sge.c ptp_lock, qdisc root_lock (sch_pie/sch_sfq/sch_red), hostap ap_handle_timer sta_table_lock, eql.c eql->lock, plus ~55 lower-priority timer callbacks enumerated but not deeply paired; hrtimer/delayed_work callbacks only partially covered. Artifact: agent-state/findings/i026.json with snapshots_checked=["s11"], execution_status=complete.
